text_plugin_synopsis: Paddle OCR PP-OCRv3 text recognition plugin for AutoJs6
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: Current README.md supports the following languages
p_introduction: The AutoJs6 Paddle OCR (PP-OCRv3) plugin adds optical character recognition powered by PaddleOCR PP-OCRv3 and ONNX Runtime, with support for screenshots, local image files, and raw image input. Since 2.0.0 it runs on ONNX Runtime instead of Paddle Lite, supports four ABIs, and comes as twelve language packages.
p_paddle_lite_edition: **Paddle Lite edition**: the Paddle Lite implementation of 1.0.x is now published separately as [Paddle OCR (PP-OCRv3 Paddle Lite)]({{ paddle_lite_plugin_url }}) (plugin ID `paddle-ocr-pp-ocrv3-paddle-lite`, variant `v3-paddle-lite`). It supports only arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a and can be installed alongside this plugin.
features: Comes as twelve language packages: Simplified Chinese, English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Latin-alphabet languages, Arabic, Cyrillic-alphabet languages, Devanagari, Telugu, Kannada, and Tamil. The Simplified Chinese package keeps the 1.0.x package name and plugin ID `paddle-ocr-pp-ocrv3`; every package uses engine `paddle-ocr` and variant `v3`.
The Arabic package returns text in reading order and lists the words of each line from right to left.
Supports screenshots, local image files, and raw ARGB_8888 image input.
Plugin information, instructions, README, and CHANGELOG support Spanish/French/Russian/Arabic/Japanese/Korean/English/Simplified Chinese/Hong Kong Traditional Chinese/Taiwan Traditional Chinese.
Based on PaddleOCR PP-OCRv3, ONNX Runtime 1.21.1, and OpenCV 4.8.0, for four ABIs: arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64, and x86.
`useSlim: true` uses detection and recognition models quantized to int8 with ONNX Runtime dynamic quantization.
`useCls: true` checks the text direction before recognition so text rotated by 180 degrees can be read; it is off by default, as in 1.0.x.

`useOpenCL` maps to NNAPI in the ONNX Runtime edition: on Android 8.1 (API 27) and later the NNAPI execution provider is used; on older versions, or when NNAPI fails to start, recognition falls back to the CPU. Whether it is faster depends on the device.
Images may contain at most 16777216 pixels; raw image buffers are limited to 64 MiB
Encoded image input is limited to 64 MiB and supports file descriptors and pipes
p_language_packages: Each language package is a separate APK, and several can be installed at the same time
p_which_to_install: Pick the package for the text you want to read: the Simplified Chinese package also reads English letters and digits and is the default recommendation; for Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Telugu, Kannada, or Tamil text, install the matching package; the Latin package covers languages such as French, German, and Spanish, the Cyrillic package covers languages such as Russian and Ukrainian, and the Devanagari package covers languages such as Hindi and Marathi; for English-only text you can also install the English package. The Devanagari, Telugu, Kannada, and Tamil models read simple words well, but conjunct letters and vowel signs written before a consonant may be wrong or out of order. Each package comes as five APKs by ABI: `arm64-v8a` (most phones), `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64`, `x86`, and `universal` (all four ABIs, the largest). Install only the one that matches your device.
p_usage_screenshot: Recognize text content in a screenshot
p_usage_local_file: Recognize text content in a local image file, using `test.png` as an example
p_usage_options: Choose a language package and set recognition options
text_comment_engine_id: Pick the Korean package by plugin ID.
text_comment_slim_cls: Use the quantized models and turn on text direction classification.
text_comment_nnapi: useOpenCL maps to NNAPI in the ONNX Runtime edition.
p_usage_options_note: Choosing a package by `profile` and the `useCls` option need AutoJs6 6.8.0 or later. Older hosts do not choose by `profile` and do not pass `useCls` on; when several language packages are installed, use `engineId` to pick one
p_api_shortcuts: `ocr.paddle()` recognizes the current screenshot by default, and `ocr.paddle(path)` recognizes a local image file
p_build_params: Build parameters come from `version.properties`, with current min SDK 24 and target SDK 37. ONNX models are not committed: before building, run `prepare_ppocrv3_assets.py` as shown above. It downloads the official PaddleOCR models, converts them to ONNX, and checks them against `libs/ppocr-android-sdk/models.provenance.json`; `--profile` accepts `zh`, `en`, `zhHant`, `ja`, `ko`, `latin`, `arabic`, `cyrillic`, `devanagari`, `te`, `ka`, `ta`, or `all`. Third-party components and licenses are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md]({{ repo_url }}/blob/master/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)
p_resource_layout: `strings.xml` provides localized plugin descriptions; `plugin_instruction.md` provides plugin instructions shown by the host. README and CHANGELOG are generated by `.python/generate_markdown.py` from JSON source files
